t: Signature eBPF: What eBPF Is: Safe Programs in the Kernel
title: Signature eBPF: What eBPF Is: Safe Programs in the Kernel
description: The Signature counterpart is the SigLens kernel tap, Manon's original introspection design. SigLens mirrors the verifier-plus-hooks architecture but adds a policy manifest: every loaded tap declares exactly which hooks, maps, and helpers it may touch, and the loader refuses taps whose manifest exceeds their signed role. The Signature design makes least-privilege structural, not advisory.

t: Signature eBPF: The Verifier: Why eBPF Cannot Crash the Kernel
title: Signature eBPF: The Verifier: Why eBPF Cannot Crash the Kernel
description: SigLens's verifier is the gatekeeper, and it checks the policy manifest too: a tap that claims a network-monitoring role but attaches to file hooks is rejected at load. The Signature design logs every rejection with the violated rule, building an audit trail of what was attempted — useful both for debugging and for spotting probing behavior.
key_facts: Bounded loops, no bad memory access

t: Signature eBPF: Maps: How Kernel Programs Talk to User Space
title: Signature eBPF: Maps: How Kernel Programs Talk to User Space
description: SigLens's maps are called ledgers, and each ledger declares its retention and cardinality caps at creation. The Signature design refuses unbounded ledgers — a tap that could grow a map forever is rejected, because observability must never become a memory-exhaustion vector.

title: Signature eBPF: CO-RE: Compile Once, Run Everywhere
